papers.title: Spatiotemporal control of Atg9 vesicle fusion in autophagosome formation.
papers.summary: Atg9 vesicles seed autophagosome formation, but must avoid premature fusion in transit. The authors show Atg23 shields Atg9 vesicles from inappropriate endomembrane fusion during transport; on arrival at the phagophore assembly site, Atg1-mediated phosphorylation of Atg9 releases Atg23, enabling Atg2 recruitment and productive autophagosome formation in yeast.

papers.title: The CENP-A chaperone complex spatially organizes centromeres.
papers.summary: Centromeres are defined by CENP-A nucleosomes, but their interphase architecture is poorly understood. The authors show the CENP-A chaperone complex organizes interphase centromeres into shell-like CENP-A/CCAN structures enclosing a chromatin-poor cavity. Chaperone presence, not its CENP-loading activity, builds this architecture, with CENP-C recruiting HJURP, revealing a structural role beyond CENP-A deposition.

papers.title: Learning stochastic dynamics and cell-fate landscapes from single-cell snapshots via optimal transport.
papers.summary: Inferring cell-fate dynamics from static single-cell snapshots is hard because stochasticity is ignored. DiffusionOT, a machine-learning framework using optimal transport and neural networks, converts stochastic differential equations into solvable landscape models from multi-timepoint transcriptomics. Benchmarked on simulated and real datasets including spatial stereo-seq, it infers trajectories, velocities, growth, gene regulatory networks, and perturbation effects.

papers.title: TCR-JANUS engager proteins enable bispecific targeting to overcome tumor heterogeneity in TCR-T cell therapy.
papers.summary: TCR-T therapy fails when tumors lose target antigen heterogeneously. The authors engineered TCR-JANUS engagers that bind both the transgenic TCR variable region and a tumor antigen (TROP2), unlike anti-CD3 bispecifics. Combined with a KRAS-G12V-specific TCR system, they enabled dual-antigen killing of divergent tumor populations with reduced T-cell exhaustion in chronic stimulation models.

papers.title: Early detection of invasive lung cancer and multiorgan metastasis by a collagen-targeted protein MRI contrast agent.
papers.summary: Early lung cancer and metastases are poorly detected by CT and biopsy. The authors identified collagen I overexpression at invasive edges of LKB1-deficient lung adenocarcinoma and built hProCA32.collagen, a collagen-targeted protein MRI agent with tenfold higher relaxivity than clinical gadolinium agents. It enabled noninvasive MRI detection of primary lung tumors and adrenal metastases, outperforming CT.

papers.title: A direct protein bridge connects the ds and ds-ss junction telomeric DNA segments in C. elegans.
papers.summary: Mammalian shelterin is complex, so the authors dissected telomere protection in C. elegans using the simpler TEBP-1/2 and POT-1 proteins. Crystallography shows POT-1's OB domain is repurposed to bind TEBP-1/2 and the telomeric ds-ssDNA junction, forming a three-way complex. Disrupting these interfaces causes telomere hyperelongation, establishing how chromosome-end protection is organized.

papers.title: Rubisco functional integrity requires a dedicated three-step maturation pathway.
papers.summary: Rubisco's catalytic subunit RbcL undergoes unusual N-terminal maturation: methionine-serine cleavage and proline acetylation. The authors define a dedicated three-step pathway—two aminopeptidases plus an acetyltransferase—coupled to chaperone-assisted assembly. This maturation enhances Rubisco activase-dependent activation and protects the enzyme from senescence-associated degradation; disrupting it reduces Rubisco accumulation and catalytic competence in plants.

papers.title: Astrocytes mediate the dopaminergic modulation of tonic GABAergic signaling in substantia nigra.
papers.summary: Dopamine modulates substantia nigra pars reticulata circuits, but mechanisms remain unclear. In mouse slices, D2 receptor signaling suppressed both phasic GABA release and tonic GABA(A)-mediated inhibition. Tonic modulation involved GAT-3 uptake regulated by D2R-expressing astrocytes, with GABA sourced from ALDH1A1 dopaminergic neurons via GAT-1, demonstrating astrocytes mediate dopaminergic control of nigral output and motor behavior.

papers.title: Metabolic regulation of calcium homeostasis via SERCA succination.
papers.summary: How metabolism regulates calcium homeostasis is unclear. The authors show fumarate succinates SERCA2b at a conserved cysteine (Cys875), inhibiting ER calcium uptake. High glucose or fumarate elevated cytosolic and mitochondrial calcium in mammalian cells, and knock-in flies bearing a succination-resistant Cys875Ser mutation were protected from hyperglycemia and reduced survival on high-sugar diet, linking glucose metabolism to calcium signaling.

papers.title: A systematic comparison of single-cell perturbation response prediction models.
papers.summary: Single-cell perturbation prediction methods lack rigorous cross-task benchmarking. The authors compared 13 methods across 25 datasets and three tasks—unseen single-gene perturbations, combinatorial interactions, and cross-cell-type transfer—using 24 metrics. Performance depended strongly on effect size and metric type; models showed conservative bias, PerturbNet led differential-expression recovery, and no method generalized across cell types.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal mapping of tertiary lymphoid structure heterogeneity shapes immune niches and clinical outcomes in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.summary: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma are heterogeneous. Integrating proteomics of 369 cases, imaging mass cytometry, and single-cell spatial transcriptomics, the authors classify intratumoral TLS as independent prognostic markers, resolve 14 spatial niches, and define a maturation continuum from aggregated to postactivated states, with CXCL12+ macrophages and CAFs orchestrating stroma-directed immunotherapy opportunities.

papers.title: BCL11B predetermines a persister state in breast cancer that is reversed by TNFα.
papers.summary: Chemoresistance causes breast cancer relapse, but its cellular origins are unclear. Using single-cell atlases, the authors identify BCL11B-marked immature basal-like cells that preferentially become drug-resistant persisters during chemotherapy. High BCL11B correlated with early relapse. TNFα emerged as a natural BCL11B inhibitor that reverses the persister state, nominating BCL11B as a predictive marker and therapeutic target.

papers.title: Substrate heterogeneity promotes cancer cell dissemination through interface roughening.
papers.summary: Tumor invasion is typically studied genetically, but physical microenvironment matters. Using microengineered patterned substrates, the authors show spatial disorder of obstacles—more than their presence—shifts cancer cells from collective to single-cell invasion, comparable to losing cell-cell adhesion. Live imaging, perturbations, and biophysical modeling reveal universality classes of invasion governed by environmental geometry, quantifying physical principles of dissemination.

papers.title: Mechanistic trade-offs between local and long-range signaling activity in natural and synthetic morphogens.
papers.summary: Hedgehog morphogens are hydrophobic yet form long-range developmental gradients. Using single-molecule tracking and synthetic ligands, the authors dissect dual lipid modifications: palmitate directly promotes receptor engagement, while cholesterol confines morphogens to the cell surface, acting as a nonsignaling co-receptor. This reveals an intrinsic trade-off between signaling potency and gradient formation with evolutionary implications.

papers.title: Widespread male-female expression imbalance of X-linked genes across phrynosomatid lizards.
papers.summary: Dosage compensation theory predicts restored diploid expression for hemizygous X-linked genes. Testing Sceloporus undulatus and nine other phrynosomatid lizards, the authors find widespread male-female expression imbalance on both ancient and neo-X regions across tissues and ages. Female-biased expression reflects female overexpression on compensated ancestral X, and male underexpression on uncompensated neo-X in S. jarrovii, challenging near-complete compensation expectations.

papers.title: Mitochondrial Fis1 tunes Rab7A activity via TBC1D15 modulating STING degradation.
papers.summary: STING innate immune signaling must be terminated by lysosomal degradation. The authors identify mitochondrial Fis1 as a key regulator: Fis1 recruits the Rab7A-GAP TBC1D15, and upon STING activation TBC1D15 relocates to the Golgi. Fis1 loss disrupts TBC1D15-Rab7A interaction, lowering Rab7A activity and impairing STING endolysosomal delivery, directly linking mitochondria to termination of innate immune signaling.

papers.title: From heart to BAT: Rethinking mouse models of human BAT.
papers.summary: Mouse brown adipose tissue research assumes the interscapular depot models human BAT. Ran and colleagues identify a heart-associated origin for mouse supraclavicular BAT, challenging this dominance. The authors argue anatomically corresponding depots may better translate thermogenic fat biology to humans, prompting reconsideration of which mouse depots are used in metabolic and thermogenesis studies.

papers.title: Integrated stress response inhibition decouples cardiotoxicity from anthracycline chemotherapy while enhancing antitumor efficacy.
papers.summary: Anthracycline chemotherapy is limited by cardiotoxicity. The authors identify the ATF4-dependent integrated stress response as central driver: doxorubicin-activated ATF4 upregulates methyltransferase METTL1, promoting m7G methylation of NLRP3 mRNA, inflammasome activation, mitochondrial damage, and pyroptosis. ISR inhibition with ISRIB protected mouse hearts while synergizing with doxorubicin against xenograft tumors, decoupling cardiotoxicity from antitumor efficacy.

papers.title: Mitochondrial Raf1 regulates glutamine catabolism.
papers.summary: RAF kinases drive mitogenic signaling, but their full protein interactions are unmapped. Proximity biotinylation revealed a mitochondrial matrix pool of RAF1. There, RAF1 associates with glutaminase across cancers in a kinase-activity-dependent manner independent of canonical MAPK signaling; matrix-targeted kinase-dead RAF1 impaired glutaminolysis and tumorigenesis, revealing a non-canonical metabolic arm of RAF signaling supporting tumor growth.

papers.title: Avl9 defines a family of DENN domain GTPase-activating proteins.
papers.summary: Many GTPase regulators remain unidentified. Computational interaction screening and functional assays show Avl9, a DENN-domain protein involved in secretion and migration, is a GTPase-activating protein for Arf1, recruited to secretory vesicles by Rab8. Avl9's Arf-GAP activity is conserved in humans and promotes migration. DENND6A, previously a Rab-GEF, also shows Arf-GAP activity toward Arl8b, defining a DENN-GAP family.

papers.title: Nucleolar dynamics are determined by the ordered assembly of the ribosome.
papers.summary: Nucleolar function depends on material properties of this condensate, but their molecular basis is unclear. Using high-throughput FRAP screening of hundreds of genes, the authors show nucleophosmin dynamics track ribosome assembly state: early pre-ribosomal intermediates slow dynamics and compact the condensate, abortive late precursors accelerate and disrupt it. NPM1-pre-ribosome interaction strength tunes nucleolar material properties directly.

papers.title: Dysfunction of caveolae in muscle disease: A cell biological perspective.
papers.summary: Caveolae are abundant sarcolemmal microdomains whose loss causes muscle diseases including caveolinopathies. This review synthesizes cell biological mechanisms linking caveolar disruption to muscle dysfunction: loss of mechanoprotection, altered signal transduction, disrupted nanoscale lipid organization, and impaired T-tubule biogenesis. The authors propose a unifying classification of disease-associated caveolin-3 variants connecting molecular defects to clinical phenotypes.

papers.title: Transketolase promotes RNF20-dependent H2BK120 ubiquitination and DNA repair through a non-enzymatic adaptor function.
papers.summary: DNA double-strand break repair requires H2BK120 ubiquitination by RNF20/RNF40. The authors identify transketolase (TKT) as a non-enzymatic adaptor in colorectal cancer cells: independent of catalytic activity, TKT bridges the FACT chromatin remodeler and RNF20, facilitating RNF20 foci formation and H2BK120ub after damage. Disrupting this axis impairs repair and radiosensitizes cells, highlighting a vulnerability in radioresistant tumors.

papers.title: Molecular basis and therapeutic potential of sortase A inhibitors as new antibiotics against MDR pathogens.
papers.summary: Sortase A anchors virulence factors to Gram-positive cell walls and is an attractive antibiotic target since it is extracellular yet nonessential. This review examines challenges of treating Gram-positive infections, the role of sortase-anchored proteins in host-pathogen interaction, and known and probable antimicrobial effects of sortase inhibition against S. aureus, S. pyogenes, B. anthracis, and L. monocytogenes.

papers.title: α-Galactosyl residues on Trypanosoma cruzi trypomastigote glycoconjugates contribute to host-cell invasion via Galectin-3 and Annexin A2-S100A10 complex.
papers.summary: Trypanosoma cruzi trypomastigotes display terminal α-Gal epitopes on GPI-anchored glycoconjugates. Affinity purification identified host Galectin-3 and Annexin A2-S100A10 as candidate receptors. Galectin-3 binds α-Gal glycoconjugates; blocking either receptor reduced macrophage infection substantially. The authors conclude α-Gal epitopes contribute to host-cell invasion through redundant receptor engagement, suggesting targets for Chagas disease vaccines, therapeutics, and biomarkers.

papers.title: Bayesian inference of gene regulatory networks at stochastic steady state.
papers.journal: Journal of the Royal Society, Interface
papers.summary: Gene regulatory network inference typically ignores biochemical dynamics. The authors present a Bayesian approach using the chemical Langevin equation at stochastic steady state with regularized horseshoe priors for sparse networks. Validated on synthetic data with known ground truth, the method infers kinetic parameters, network structure, and regulatory cycles without transient observations, providing interpretability and structural identifiability.

papers.title: HOG pathway-dependent protection against impaired complex sphingolipid biosynthesis involves Fmp48-mediated suppression of mitochondria-dependent ROS accumulation.
papers.summary: Repressing Aur1, yeast inositol phosphorylceramide synthase, lowers complex sphingolipids, accumulates ceramide, and causes death. The HOG pathway protects against this. Here Fmp48, Uip4, and Mga1 overexpression suppressed cell death without restoring sphingolipid levels. Aur1 repression caused mitochondria-dependent ROS accumulation; Fmp48 overexpression suppressed ROS and death, identifying HOG-dependent cytoprotection acting through mitochondrial ROS control.

papers.title: The VPS9-family GEF VINE activates Ypt10 in a late endosomal Rab cascade.
papers.summary: Rab cascades coordinate endosomal maturation through GEFs and GAPs. The yeast VINE complex, a VPS9-family GEF, inactivates Rab5-homolog Vps21 and activates Ypt10 at late endosomes downstream of Vps21. VINE-dependent Ypt10 recruitment of Mon1-Ccz1 enhances Ypt7 activation, defining a Vps21-VINE-Ypt10 module that couples Rab5 inactivation to Rab7 activation for precise vacuolar protein traffic.

papers.title: Reversibility of Nuclear and 3D Genomic Changes in Non-Cancerous Fibroblasts After Constricted Migration.
papers.summary: Cancer cells undergo stable nuclear and 3D genome changes after constricted migration, but non-cancerous cells are unstudied. Fibroblasts migrating through constrictions showed nuclear deformation and compartment-level 3D genome alterations rearranging migration-related genes. Unlike cancer cells, most changes reverted after proliferation, though some persisted. Non-cancerous migratory cells are equally susceptible but recover more readily than transformed cells.

papers.title: Identification and validation of oxidative stress-related immune signatures in Hepatitis B Virus associated acute liver failure based on WGCNA and machine learning.
papers.summary: Immune infiltration and oxidative stress interact in hepatitis B-associated acute liver failure, but this combination is unexplored. Integrating WGCNA and machine learning on public datasets, the authors identify CLU, APOH, AMBP, and GPX8 as oxidative stress-immune signature genes validated by ROC analysis, enriched in metabolic processes, and connected via miRNA-TF networks to candidate drugs including CLU-targeting agents.

papers.title: Effects of exercise on muscle strength and characteristics in rheumatic diseases and sarcopenia: Protocol for the Care for Muscle (C4M) Study.
papers.summary: Muscle weakness is prevalent in rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, and sarcopenia, but exercise response varies. This protocol describes a two-arm randomized trial of 69 patients comparing eight weeks of supervised endurance versus strength training. Outcomes include isokinetic strength, 3D ultrasound muscle morphology, mitochondrial respirometry on biopsies, and systemic inflammation, aiming to personalize training based on intramuscular pathology.

papers.title: HIV-1 lentivirus with VSV-G envelope: Complex N glycosylation governs shifts in aggregation and infectivity state at close to physiological pH, serum, and Ca2+ levels.
papers.summary: VSV-G pseudotyped HIV-1 lentivectors used in gene therapy carry complex N-glycans. Dynamic light scattering revealed three solution states—self-aggregated, dispersed, and calcium-induced aggregated—switching at near-physiological pH, serum, and calcium levels, with significantly different infectivity. Enzymatic removal of terminal sialic acid and galactose abolished switching, implying envelope glycosylation enables environmental sensing with consequences for vector infectivity.

papers.title: UPLC-MS metabolite profiling and antioxidant efficacy of Neopestalotiopsisclavispora isolated from Oroxylum indicum (L.) Kurz Stem Bark.
papers.summary: Endophytic fungi produce bioactive metabolites. The authors profiled Neopestalotiopsis clavispora from Oroxylum indicum stem bark by UPLC-MS, identifying cimicifoetiside B as predominant metabolite, and showed moderate DPPH radical scavenging. In gamma-irradiated mice, 100 mg/kg extract elevated liver superoxide dismutase activity, with docking and molecular dynamics supporting cimicifoetiside B-SOD interaction, suggesting antioxidant potential warranting further study.

papers.title: Whole exome sequencing and cluster analysis reveal that EPB41L4A mutation may trigger tooth agenesis.
papers.summary: Non-syndromic tooth agenesis has known genetic causes but unexplained cases remain. Whole-exome sequencing of 18 congenitally edentulous subjects followed by hierarchical and fuzzy clustering against known tooth agenesis genes showed EPB41L4A clustering with established disease genes. EPB41L4A, involved in Wnt signaling, is proposed as a candidate gene warranting further investigation for tooth agenesis diagnosis and counseling.

papers.title: Codon bias variation in Staphylococcus aureus.
papers.summary: Synonymous codon usage bias in Staphylococcus aureus is underexplored. The authors quantified codon adaptation indices for 2,565 genes against publicly available closed genomes, finding variation within and between isolates. Ribosome-associated genes showed consistently high CAI, and CAI correlated moderately with in vitro protein expression. Codon bias constitutes a source of genetic variation between S. aureus isolates globally.

papers.title: miR-191 affects skeletal muscle differentiation by regulating Wwp1 in mouse myoblasts.
papers.summary: Skeletal muscle atrophy complicates COPD and cancer. Plasma miRNA profiling identified altered miR-191 in COPD patients. In mouse myoblasts and cardiotoxin-injured muscle, miR-191 negatively correlated with Wwp1; miR-191 mimics suppressed myogenic regulators and mTOR pathway genes. The authors show miR-191 directly targets the Wwp1 3'UTR, defining a miR-191/Wwp1 axis regulating skeletal muscle differentiation.

papers.title: Cardiomyocyte hypertrophy co-localizes with accumulation of hyaluronan in cMyBPC+/- mice hearts.
papers.summary: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy involves altered glucose metabolism that could drive hyaluronan synthesis. In cMyBPC+/- mice, cardiac hyaluronan accumulated in a patchy pattern that colocalized with enlarged cardiomyocytes, with elevated hyaluronan synthase 2 expression. Eleven months of metoprolol or propranolol did not prevent hyaluronan accumulation or hypertrophy, though propranolol maintained synthase 2 at wild-type levels while increasing synthase 3.

papers.title: ANCA testing strategies: A single centre experience over the past decade in a large teaching hospital in the Netherlands.
papers.summary: ANCA testing consensus derives from tertiary centers with high vasculitis prevalence. This Dutch teaching hospital analyzed 5,518 patients tested between 2012-2023; only 5.2% were positive and 63% of positives lacked vasculitis. ELISA as first test showed best negative and positive predictive value, with second testing recommended when clinical suspicion conflicts with results, improving specificity in secondary care settings.

papers.title: First insights into the miRNA landscape of Tursiops truncatus milk reveal shared dominant microRNA families with terrestrial mammals.
papers.summary: Marine mammal milk microRNAs are uncharacterized. The authors report the first bottlenose dolphin milk miRNA landscape: 186 conserved families in the genome, 119 miRNAs detected in milk, dominated by miR-148, let-7, miR-8, and miR-21 comprising over 70% of reads. These mirror dominant families in terrestrial mammal milk, suggesting qualitative similarity in milk miRNA repertoires across mammals.

papers.title: Genome-wide identification and expression analysis of the ZIP (ZRT, IRT-like protein) family in Solanum lycopersicum.
papers.summary: ZIP family transporters mediate iron, zinc, manganese, and copper uptake in plants. The authors identify 14 SlZIP genes in tomato across three phylogenetic clades with conserved exon/intron organization, whose promoters contain iron- and copper-deficiency-responsive cis-elements. Expression analysis under metal deficiency showed SlIRT1/2 and SlZIP4 induced by iron limitation, SlZIP2/11 by copper, and SlZIP13/14 by manganese deficiency.

papers.title: Genetic Testing Unveils a Novel Thrombospondin-1 Domain Containing Protein 1 Gene Variant as the Cause of Chronic Edema in a 79-Year-Old Woman.
papers.summary: A 79-year-old woman with lifelong unexplained peripheral edema underwent whole-genome sequencing after excluding common etiologies. A novel homozygous splice-site variant in THSD1, previously linked to non-immune hydrops fetalis, was identified. This first reported elderly THSD1 case suggests the disease can present in late adulthood and highlights genetic testing's value in chronic unexplained edema, though causality is not definitively established.

papers.title: A Novel De Novo STAG1 Variant at the RAD21 Binding Interface Is Associated With Hypoglycemia, Recurrent Fever, Immunodeficiency and Features of Classical Cohesinopathies.
papers.summary: Cohesinopathies classically involve developmental delay, intellectual disability, and feeding difficulties. A 5-year-old boy presented these plus hypoglycemia, recurrent fever, and immunodeficiency. Trio exome sequencing identified a novel de novo STAG1 missense variant at the RAD21 binding interface; molecular dynamics simulations showed conformational changes matching likely pathogenic variants, expanding the STAG1-related cohesinopathy phenotypic and molecular spectrum.

papers.title: Acteoside alleviates high glucose-induced ROS accumulation and ferroptosis in ARPE-19 cells by activating the NRF2 signaling pathway.
papers.summary: Diabetic retinopathy involves retinal pigment epithelial ferroptosis. In high-glucose ARPE-19 cells and a mouse model, acteoside reversed ferroptosis markers—iron accumulation, lipid peroxidation, reduced GPX4 and SLC7A11—by promoting NRF2 nuclear translocation; NRF2 silencing abolished protection. Retinal damage in diabetic mice was alleviated dose-dependently, establishing acteoside as a NRF2-activating anti-ferroptotic candidate for diabetic retinopathy.

papers.title: Evaluation of curcumin as an exploratory pharmacological tool for modulating dysregulated molecular pathways in cellular models of Huntington's disease.
papers.summary: Huntington's disease involves mutant huntingtin aggregation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and stress signaling. In cellular HD models, curcumin reduced mHTT aggregation and PERK-eIF2α signaling by elevating autophagic clearance, increased ATP, partially restored PGC-1α and NRF1 expression, reduced ROS and H3K27me3, and abrogated inflammatory responses in patient-derived lymphoblasts, providing mechanistic insight into curcumin's modulation of multiple HD-relevant pathways.

papers.title: Molecular dissection and functional characterization of the liguleless1 gene for manipulation of leaf angle in maize.
papers.summary: Recessive liguleless1 reduces maize leaf angle, aiding high-density planting. Sequencing the 5,560 bp gene in wild-type and mutant inbreds revealed a 130 bp Tourist MITE insertion deleting 157 C-terminal amino acids. The authors developed a co-dominant indel marker distinguishing alleles, validated in F2 populations with expected 3:1 leaf-angle segregation, plus 11 gene-based markers classifying 48 inbreds into 35 haplotypes for breeding.

papers.title: Discovery and evolution of endogenous retroviruses in the genome of crab-eating macaque (Macaca fascicularis).
papers.summary: Endogenous retroviruses in the crab-eating macaque genome were uncharacterized despite its biomedical importance. Using a chromosome-level assembly, homology-based screening identified 106 relatively intact proviral loci across all chromosomes, classified phylogenetically into beta-, gamma-, and unclassified lineages. LTR divergence dating revealed multiple waves of retroviral activity, providing a curated reference set for studying ERV evolution in an endangered primate model.

papers.title: TET2 promotes monocyte inflammatory activation in asthma via ALKBH5-m6A regulation and PI3K signaling: evidence from m6A-SNP and single-cell analyses.
papers.summary: Asthma-associated non-coding variants' functions are mostly unclear. Integrating GWAS, m6A-SNP annotation, and single-cell data, the authors identify TET2 as an m6A-regulated gene upregulated in asthmatic monocytes. Inflammatory stimulation induces ALKBH5, reducing TET2 mRNA m6A and increasing TET2 protein, enhancing PI3K/AKT signaling and cytokine production. The ALKBH5-m6A-TET2 axis emerges as a therapeutic target for monocyte-driven airway inflammation.

papers.title: DOT1L-mediated H3K79me3 of ITCH promotes AURKA ubiquitination to suppress ECM degradation in osteoarthritis.
papers.summary: Osteoarthritis involves chondrocyte extracellular matrix degradation lacking effective therapy. The authors define a DOT1L/ITCH/AURKA axis: IL-1β upregulated AURKA while downregulating DOT1L and ITCH. DOT1L-mediated H3K79me3 at the ITCH promoter increased ITCH, which ubiquitinated and degraded AURKA, suppressing ECM degradation. DOT1L overexpression via lentivirus alleviated cartilage degeneration in a rat osteoarthritis model, identifying an epigenetic-PTM regulatory mechanism.

papers.title: ACE2 and Parkinsonism‑related bone metabolic alterations: signaling pathways and hub gene analysis.
papers.summary: Parkinson's disease co-occurs with bone loss, but mechanisms are unclear. Using MPTP-treated ACE2-deficient mice, the authors found ACE2 deletion reduced Wnt, β-catenin, BMP, and IGF-1 signaling in brain and bone while elevating RANKL-pathway mediators. WGCNA identified hub genes linked to synaptic dysfunction and inflammation with diagnostic accuracy in public datasets, supporting a potential bone-brain axis requiring further causal validation.

papers.title: Circular RNAs orchestrate integrated post-transcriptional responses to combined heat and drought stress in rice.
papers.summary: Circular RNAs' roles in rice under combined heat and drought stress are unexplored. Reanalyzing strand-specific RNA-seq, the authors identify 208 high-confidence circRNAs with stress-dependent circularization, predominantly exonic with negative-strand bias. Host genes implicate protein folding, RNA degradation, and amino acid catabolism. Seven circRNAs were stress-induced, with osa-miR414, miR1439, and miR2919 as predicted network hubs coordinating post-transcriptional stress responses.

papers.title: Dose-Dependent Hepatic Alterations Following Glyphosate Exposure in Female Wistar Rats: Oxidative Stress, Intracellular Cyclic Nucleotide Alterations, Apoptosis, and VEGF.
papers.summary: Glyphosate herbicides may harm liver, but cyclic nucleotide and VEGF roles are unclear. Female Wistar rats received 250-1000 mg/kg/day glyphosate orally for 30 days. Dose-dependent increases occurred in oxidant status, TNF-α, IL-1β, caspase-3, VEGF, and Bax/Bcl-2 ratio, with decreased antioxidant status and cyclic nucleotides plus progressive histopathological changes, linking glyphosate hepatotoxicity to coordinated oxidative, inflammatory, apoptotic, and vascular alterations.
